lessons.title: Architecture Scenarios
lessons.summary: Understand architecture scenarios by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Requirements
paragraphs: Functional requirement: States what behavior the system must provide.
Quality requirement: States measurable properties such as latency or reliability.
Constraint: Limits permitted design choices.
Acceptance criterion: Defines observable evidence that a requirement is met.

sections.title: Component boundaries
paragraphs: API boundary: Defines validated requests and responses between callers and services.
Persistence boundary: Owns durable data and migration behavior.
Inference boundary: Owns model execution and its limits.
Presentation boundary: Owns readable interaction and accessible display.

sections.title: Architecture decisions
paragraphs: Tradeoff analysis: Compare benefits and costs under stated requirements.
Assumption record: Make unverified premises explicit.
Baseline: Establish the simplest workable comparison.
Evidence: Use measured results to justify a decision.

sections.title: Reliability design
paragraphs: Timeout: Bound waiting for one operation.
Retry policy: Repeat only eligible work under bounded conditions.
Idempotency: Prevent duplicated logical effects.
Fallback: Offer a supported alternative when the primary path fails.

sections.title: Security and operations
paragraphs: Threat boundary: Separates trust levels and limits authority.
Telemetry: Provides evidence of actual operational behavior.
Release gate: Requires defined checks before rollout.
Recovery plan: Defines restoration or rollback after failure.

sections.title: Model concepts
paragraphs: Token: A tokenizer-defined unit is not universally one word.
Context: The model request has bounded input/output capacity under its contract.
Embedding: A representation supports similarity comparisons rather than guarantees truth.
Structured output: A format contract still needs semantic validation.

sections.title: Retrieval concepts
paragraphs: Chunk: A retrievable unit derived from source content.
Index: A searchable organization of records.
Reranker: Reorders a candidate set for relevance.
Citation: Connects an answer claim with its source.

sections.title: Agent concepts
paragraphs: Workflow: Code determines a known execution path.
Agent: A model selects actions within enforced constraints.
Tool call: A request to a capability still needs host validation and execution.
Observation: Actual feedback informs later decisions.

sections.title: Adaptation concepts
paragraphs: Prompting: Changes instructions without training weights.
Fine-tuning: Updates learned parameters using an objective.
LoRA: Uses trainable low-rank updates on a compatible base.
Quantization: Uses lower-precision representation with measured tradeoffs.

sections.title: Evidence in answers
paragraphs: Definition: States what a concept means precisely.
Example: Demonstrates the concept in a concrete case.
Tradeoff: Explains benefits and costs under constraints.
Limitation: States where a claim or approach does not apply.

lessons.title: Coding Concepts
lessons.summary: Understand coding concepts by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Complexity
paragraphs: Constant time: Work does not grow with input size under the stated operation model.
Linear time: Work grows proportionally with input size.
Quadratic time: Work grows with the square of input size.
Logarithmic time: Work grows with repeated proportional reduction of the search space.

sections.title: Collections
paragraphs: Dictionary: Maps keys to values.
Set: Stores unique elements for membership and set operations.
Queue: Processes elements in first-in-first-out order.
Stack: Processes elements in last-in-first-out order.

sections.title: Function design
paragraphs: Pure computation: Returns a result without intended external effects for the same explicit inputs.
Validation: Rejects inputs that violate the contract.
Side effect: Changes external state such as storage or a network service.
Error propagation: Makes failure visible to the caller.

sections.title: Concurrency concepts
paragraphs: Race condition: Outcome depends on uncontrolled ordering of competing operations.
Atomic operation: An operation is indivisible under its defined concurrency model.
Mutual exclusion: Restricts concurrent access to a protected critical section.
Idempotency: Repeated logical execution has no additional intended effect.

sections.title: Testing
paragraphs: Boundary case: Exercises limits such as zero, empty or maximum-size inputs.
Regression case: Retains a previously failing scenario after it is fixed.
Integration case: Exercises interactions between components.
Property check: Verifies a general invariant over multiple inputs.

lessons.title: Interview Practice
lessons.summary: Understand interview practice by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Clarification
paragraphs: Goal: Identify the outcome the interviewer wants designed or explained.
Constraint: Identify limits such as privacy, hardware or deployment rules.
Scale: Identify workload size and concurrency assumptions.
Success measure: Define measurable evidence that the design works.

sections.title: Answer structure
paragraphs: Definition: Explain a concept's meaning before using it.
Concrete example: Demonstrate behavior in a specific scenario.
Tradeoff: Compare consequences of alternatives.
Qualification: State assumptions and limits without unsupported certainty.

sections.title: Scenario reasoning
paragraphs: Evidence gathering: Obtain facts before drawing conclusions.
Failure isolation: Locate the component where behavior diverges from the contract.
Alternative comparison: Evaluate feasible options against requirements.
Decision rationale: Explain why a chosen option fits stated constraints.

sections.title: Coding discussion
paragraphs: Input contract: State expected values and permitted shapes.
Algorithm: Describe the steps used to compute the result.
Complexity: Explain how resource requirements scale.
Verification: Demonstrate cases and invariants supporting correctness.

sections.title: Readiness claims
paragraphs: Knowledge evidence: Quiz results demonstrate performance on sampled conceptual questions.
Practice feedback: Feedback helps improve explanation but is not a hiring decision.
Professional experience: Actual applied work supports claims about execution experience.
Honest uncertainty: State missing knowledge rather than invent facts or experience.
